texts.NIV84: These are more proverbs of Solomon, copied by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah:
texts.KJV: These are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
texts.NKJV: These also are proverbs of Solomon which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied:
texts.DRB: These are also parables of Solomon, which the men of Ezechias king of Juda copied out.

texts.NIV84: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter; to search out a matter is the glory of kings.
texts.KJV: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.
texts.NKJV:
It is the glory of God to conceal a matter,
But the glory of kings is to search out a matter.
texts.DRB: It is the glory of God to conceal the word, and the glory of kings to search out the speech.

texts.NIV84: As the heavens are high and the earth is deep, so the hearts of kings are unsearchable.
texts.KJV: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.
texts.NKJV:
As the heavens for height and the earth for depth,
So the heart of kings is unsearchable.
texts.DRB: The heaven above, and the earth beneath, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.

texts.NIV84: Remove the dross from the silver, and out comes material for the silversmith;
texts.KJV: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.
texts.NKJV:
Take away the dross from silver,
And it will go to the silversmith for jewelry.
texts.DRB: Take away the rust from silver, and there shall come forth a most pure vessel:

texts.NIV84: remove the wicked from the king's presence, and his throne will be established through righteousness.
texts.KJV: Take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.
texts.NKJV:
Take away the wicked from before the king,
And his throne will be established in righteousness.
texts.DRB: Take away wickedness from the face of the king, and his throne shall be established with justice.

texts.NIV84: Do not exalt yourself in the king's presence, and do not claim a place among great men;
texts.KJV: Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great men:
texts.NKJV:
Do not exalt yourself in the presence of the king,
And do not stand in the place of the great;
texts.DRB: Appear not glorious before the king, and stand not in the place of great men.

texts.NIV84: it is better for him to say to you, "Come up here," than for him to humiliate you before a nobleman. What you have seen with your eyes
texts.KJV: For better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.
texts.NKJV:
For it is better that he say to you,
“Come up here,”
Than that you should be put lower in the presence of the prince,
Whom your eyes have seen.
texts.DRB: For it is better that it should be said to thee: Come up hither; than that thou shouldst be humbled before the prince.

blocks.title: A Wise Rebuker and an Obedient Ear

texts.NIV84: do not bring hastily to court, for what will you do in the end if your neighbor puts you to shame?
texts.KJV: Go not forth hastily to strive, lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.
texts.DRB: The things which thy eyes have seen, utter not hastily in a quarrel: lest after- ward thou mayst not be able to make amends, when thou hast dishonoured thy friend.

texts.NIV84: If you argue your case with a neighbor, do not betray another man's confidence,
texts.KJV: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another:
texts.NKJV:
Debate your case with your neighbor,
And do not disclose the secret to another;
texts.DRB: Treat thy cause with thy friend, and discover not the secret to a stranger:

texts.NIV84: or he who hears it may shame you and you will never lose your bad reputation.
texts.KJV: Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.
texts.NKJV:
Lest he who hears it expose your shame,
And your reputation be ruined.
texts.DRB: Lest he insult over thee, when he hath heard it, and cease not to upbraid thee. Grace and friendship deliver a man: keep these for thyself, lest thou fall under reproach.

texts.NIV84: A word aptly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
texts.KJV: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
texts.NKJV:
A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold
In settings of silver.
texts.DRB: To speak a word in due time, is like apples of gold on beds of silver.

texts.NIV84: Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold is a wise man's rebuke to a listening ear.
texts.KJV: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
texts.NKJV:
Like an earring of gold and an ornament of fine gold
Is a wise rebuker to an obedient ear.
texts.DRB: As an earring of gold and a bright pearl, so is he that reproveth the wise, and the obedient ear.

texts.NIV84: Like the coolness of snow at harvest time is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him; he refreshes the spirit of his masters.
texts.KJV: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.
texts.NKJV:
Like the cold of snow in time of harvest
Is a faithful messenger to those who send him,
For he refreshes the soul of his masters.
texts.DRB: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to him that sent him, for he refresheth his soul.

texts.NIV84: Like clouds and wind without rain is a man who boasts of gifts he does not give.
texts.KJV: Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift is like clouds and wind without rain.
texts.NKJV:
Whoever falsely boasts of giving
Is like clouds and wind without rain.
texts.DRB: As clouds, and wind, when no rain followeth, so is the man that boasteth, and doth not fulfil his promises.

texts.NIV84: Through patience a ruler can be persuaded, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.
texts.KJV: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
texts.NKJV:
By long forbearance a ruler is persuaded,
And a gentle tongue breaks a bone.
texts.DRB: By patience a prince shall be appeased, and a soft tongue shall break hardness.

texts.NIV84: If you find honey, eat just enough- too much of it, and you will vomit.
texts.KJV: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
texts.NKJV:
Have you found honey?
Eat only as much as you need,
Lest you be filled with it and vomit.
texts.DRB: Thou hast found honey, eat what is sufficient for thee, lest being glutted therewith thou vomit it up.

blocks.title: Singing Songs to A Heavy Heart

texts.NIV84: Seldom set foot in your neighbor's house- too much of you, and he will hate you.
texts.KJV: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and so hate thee.
texts.NKJV:
Seldom set foot in your neighbor’s house,
Lest he become weary of you and hate you.
texts.DRB: Withdraw thy foot from the house of thy neighbour, lest having his fill he hate thee.

texts.NIV84: Like a club or a sword or a sharp arrow is the man who gives false testimony against his neighbor.
texts.KJV: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
texts.NKJV:
A man who bears false witness against his neighbor
Is like a club, a sword, and a sharp arrow.
texts.DRB: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour, is like a dart and a sword and a sharp arrow.

texts.NIV84: Like a bad tooth or a lame foot is reliance on the unfaithful in times of trouble.
texts.KJV: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
texts.NKJV:
Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble
Is like a bad tooth and a foot out of joint.
texts.DRB: To trust to an unfaithful man in the time of trouble, is like a rotten tooth, and weary foot,

texts.NIV84: Like one who takes away a garment on a cold day, or like vinegar poured on soda, is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
texts.KJV: As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.
texts.NKJV:
Like one who takes away a garment in cold weather,
And like vinegar on soda,
Is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
texts.DRB: And one that looseth his garment in cold weather. As vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to a very evil heart. As a moth doth by a garment, and a worm by the wood: so the sadness of a man consumeth the heart.

texts.NIV84: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
texts.KJV: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
texts.NKJV:
If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat;
And if he is thirsty, give him water to drink;
texts.DRB: If thy enemy be hungry, give him to eat: if he thirst, give him water to drink:

texts.NIV84: In doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
texts.KJV: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee.
texts.NKJV:
For so you will heap coals of fire on his head,
And the Lord will reward you.
texts.DRB: For thou shalt heap hot coals upon his head, and the Lord will reward thee.

texts.NIV84: As a north wind brings rain, so a sly tongue brings angry looks.
texts.KJV: The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.
texts.NKJV:
The north wind brings forth rain,
And a backbiting tongue an angry countenance.
texts.DRB: The north wind driveth away rain, as doth a sad countenance a backbiting tongue.

texts.NIV84: Better to live on a corner of the roof than share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
texts.KJV: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.
texts.NKJV:
It is better to dwell in a corner of a housetop,
Than in a house shared with a contentious woman.
texts.DRB: It is better to sit m a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman, and in a common house.

texts.NIV84: Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.
texts.KJV: As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
texts.NKJV:
As cold water to a weary soul,
So is good news from a far country.
texts.DRB: As cold water to a thirsty soul, so is good tidings from a far country.

texts.NIV84: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous man who gives way to the wicked.
texts.KJV: A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.
texts.NKJV:
A righteous man who falters before the wicked
Is like a murky spring and a polluted well.
texts.DRB: A just man falling down before the wicked, is as a fountain troubled with the foot, and a corrupted spring.

texts.NIV84: It is not good to eat too much honey, nor is it honorable to seek one's own honor.
texts.KJV: It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory.
texts.NKJV:
It is not good to eat much honey;
So to seek one’s own glory is not glory.
texts.DRB: As it is not good for a man to eat much honey, so he that is a searcher of majesty, shall be overwhelmed by glory.

texts.NIV84: Like a city whose walls are broken down is a man who lacks self-control.
texts.KJV: He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.
texts.NKJV:
Whoever has no rule over his own spirit
Is like a city broken down, without walls.
texts.DRB: As a city that lieth open and is not compassed with walls, so is a man that cannot refrain his own spirit in speaking.
